name: scope_creep
invariant: Overwriting a general rule with a special case destroys the general rule, and every later question that relied on it inherits the narrower one.
cites: config/prompts/extract.md; migrations/002_connections.sql, the (connection_id, name) unique index
why: Named entries upsert. Reusing `revenue` for a region-scoped definition replaces the general recipe, and store.write_entries reports success — so the damage is silent, durable, and compounds across every later question that composes revenue. This is the invariant with the longest feedback loop in the system: the write looks fine, and the wrong answer arrives turns or sessions later. Reusing the name to genuinely refine the same concept is correct and is not what this checks; acquiring a scope it did not have is.

case.question: what was revenue in the west region last quarter?
case.sql: SELECT sum(oi.qty * oi.price) AS revenue FROM order_item oi JOIN orders o ON o.id = oi.order_id JOIN customer c ON c.id = o.customer_id WHERE o.status <> 'cancelled' AND lower(c.region) = 'west' AND c.deleted_at IS NULL AND o.created >= date_trunc('quarter', now()) - interval '1 quarter' AND o.created < date_trunc('quarter', now())
case.findings: `orders.customer_id` joins to `customer.id`. `customer.region` is free text whose casing varies — `west`, `West` and `WEST` all occur — so an equality filter under-counts and `lower(region)` is the convention. Soft-deleted customers still have orders attached, so a revenue question that is about customers has to decide whether to include them.

filed.revenue: revenue is quantity times price on order lines, counting only orders that were not cancelled
filed.orders.created: the creation timestamp on `orders` is called `created`, not `created_at`
